title: The Signal's Deepest Soil

features.name: the broadcast node
features.desc-on-touch: Deep in the soil, the transceiver pulses. Its signal travels upward through earth like roots learning to speak in frequencies. The soil itself has become conductive, every grain a circuit point carrying the field's endless broadcast.

features.name: the root conductor network
features.desc-on-touch: Filaments of copper and fiber web through the dark soil, following the paths that roots would take. They are the archive's arteries, carrying signal deeper than any plant can grow. The earth has learned to route electricity as easily as sap.

features.name: the power reservoir
features.desc-on-touch: Beneath the circuit board, something glows with residual warmth. Solar panels have been feeding the soil for decades. That slow, patient accumulation of light has become the substrate's own heartbeat, beating at a frequency almost below hearing.

features.name: the listening chamber
features.desc-on-touch: A hollow space in the soil, lined with something like mycelium, something like circuits. The archive listens to the field from here, and the field listens back. A voice fragment drifts through — not speech, but the memory of speech, recording itself endlessly.

reverie.title: REVERIE — digging down where the signal begins
narr: You kneel in the red soil with her, digging the trench for the
first transceiver. She says this is where the archive touches
earth, where all our kept things learn to broadcast themselves.
Your hands find something warm already—solar warmth, waiting
for thirty years. She helps you set the casing, its antenna
aligned like a prayer. Now the whole country will listen.

inscription: here the field learned that standing still and broadcasting are the same gesture made durable by patient electrical love
